subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 32-year-old man with active tuberculosis begins isoniazid therapy. One month later he reports numbness and tingling of both feet, and serum pyridoxine is low. His liver function tests are normal.
question: Deficiency of pyridoxal phosphate would most directly impair which of the following reactions?

options.text: Transfer of an amino group from alanine to alpha-ketoglutarate

explanation_correct: Pyridoxal phosphate is the cofactor for transaminases such as alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase, which transfer alpha-amino groups from amino acids to alpha-ketoglutarate. Isoniazid interferes with pyridoxine metabolism, so transamination and other pyridoxal phosphate-dependent reactions, including decarboxylation of dopamine and synthesis of GABA, are impaired.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pyruvate carboxylase requires biotin, not pyridoxal phosphate.
explanation_incorrect.B: The alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex requires thiamine pyrophosphate and lipoic acid, not pyridoxal phosphate.
explanation_incorrect.C: Phenylalanine hydroxylase requires tetrahydrobiopterin and iron; it is not pyridoxal phosphate-dependent.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase requires vitamin C (ascorbate), not pyridoxal phosphate.

educationalObjective: Pyridoxal phosphate is the essential cofactor for transaminases such as alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase.
